findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Ground S6 transition replay in prior art (or justify its novelty vs. the established 'attempt direct target then drift' approach) and name the concrete source of 'rebar's recorded hop sequence' — the reconciler currently records status labels, not a transition-hop history, so the 'reuses machinery that already exists' claim must be substantiated or corrected.
evidence: Plan Approach: 'Non-allowed transitions additionally attempt replay of rebar's own recorded hop sequence (anchored on Jira's current status, bounded give-up->drift) before drifting' and the framing 'each reusing machinery that already exists'
search_files for 'status_history' and 'recorded hop' in the reconciler returned no matches — no existing hop-sequence recording machinery
acli.py:491-545 transition_issue_by_name performs a single direct transition lookup (find one transition reaching target from current state), not a path/replay walk

Web search for state-machine transition path-replay in issue-tracker sync tools returned no established pattern; mature sync tooling (Exalate marketplace listing) maps/sets target status or drifts rather than replaying a hop sequence
findings.finding: The S6 'transition replay' pattern is a novel architectural/algorithmic approach whose prior art is not considered and whose 'reuses machinery that already exists' claim is unsubstantiated: the reconciler records status LABELS, not a transition-hop history (no status_history / hop-recording machinery exists in src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/), and the existing acli.transition_issue_by_name does a single direct attempt, not a replayed sequence.
findings.location: Approach (transition replay sentence) and Child S6 — 'Transition replay adds the direct->replay->drift fallback to the dispatcher'; AC line 'A non-allowed transition is attempted by replay of rebar's recorded hops'
scenarios: A target workflow disallows the direct transition rebar wants, forcing the replay path — the implementer discovers there is no recorded hop sequence to replay and must design a source of intermediate states from scratch
A reviewer or future maintainer assumes replay reuses existing machinery per the Approach and under-scopes S6

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add (assign to a child, most naturally S1/bfe7 or each axis child) a test asserting the composed/resolved default map equals the current hardcoded constants (LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA / LOCAL_TYPE_TO_JIRA / RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK / LOCAL_PRIORITY_TO_JIRA), satisfying parent AC1's second oracle.
evidence: Parent AC1: 'verified by the existing reconciler suite passing unchanged and a test asserting the composed default map equals the current hardcoded constants.'

bfe7 ACs verify test_reserved_section_not_unknown, test_perkey_merge_precedence, test_vocab_lists_replace_wholesale, test_config_effect_contrast (overlay != default), test_validate_fails_closed, test_core_is_provider_neutral — none assert composed-default == hardcoded constants.
438a AC4: 'The value_maps↔config parity test remains green' — this is the two hardcoded copies agreeing, not resolved-default↔hardcoded identity.
findings.finding: Parent AC1 requires TWO oracles — the existing reconciler suite passing unchanged AND 'a test asserting the composed default map equals the current hardcoded constants' — but no sibling's acceptance criteria assert the composed/resolved default map is byte-identical to the current hardcoded constants. bfe7 verifies only that an overlay DIFFERS from the default (test_config_effect_contrast) and per-key merge precedence; 438a keeps the value_maps↔config parity test green (two hardcoded copies agreeing with each other, not the resolved-default equalling the hardcoded literals). The specific identity assertion the parent names is covered by no child.
scenarios: A refactor silently perturbs the built-in default injection (e.g. a key dropped during the value_maps→injected-fallback conversion) so a no-override project no longer maps byte-for-identical to today; no test catches it because no child asserts composed-default == hardcoded-constants.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC to bfe7 (or to each axis child) of the form 'resolve_for_project with no overrides yields a map == the injected built-in default constant' plus a top-level 'composed default == the pre-seam hardcoded constants' assertion.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an AC/test to d458 asserting that when a target transition is illegal/drifts, rebar's own local status transition is retained unrestricted (the drift never rolls back or blocks the local hop).
evidence: Parent AC5: '...never restricting rebar's local transitions — verified per child.'
Parent Approach: 'rebar's own transitions and hierarchy are never restricted by a target's rules.'
d458 ACs cover replay end-state, unclean-hop drift, re-anchor idempotence, no-self-heal — none assert that rebar's local transition is left unrestricted when the target forbids it.
findings.finding: Parent AC5 requires the transition behavior to be verified as 'never restricting rebar's local transitions' (the parent Approach states 'rebar's own transitions and hierarchy are never restricted by a target's rules'), but d458's acceptance criteria verify only replay-reaches-end-state, unclean-hop-drifts, re-anchor idempotence, and no-self-heal. No sibling AC asserts that a target's transition rules never restrict/block rebar's own local status transitions. The remainder clause of AC5 is unnamed and unverified.
scenarios: A future change makes a drifted/illegal target transition also block or roll back rebar's own local hop; because no test asserts local transitions are never restricted, the regression ships silently while replay/drift tests still pass.
findings.suggested_fix: In d458, add 'A drift/illegal target transition never mutates or restricts rebar's local status — verified by test_transition_replay.py::test_local_transition_unrestricted.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Choose a non-colliding name for the new config-suggestion command (e.g. `rebar bridge probe-config` / `rebar bridge suggest-config`) or explicitly reconcile it with the existing `bridge-probe`->`check-access` alias, and note the chosen spelling in S8.

findings.finding: The proposed new subcommand `rebar bridge probe` collides in name with the already-shipped `rebar bridge-probe` compatibility alias and is easily confused with the canonical `rebar bridge check-access` (the former `bridge-probe`).
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — 'A `rebar bridge probe` command'; child S8

Docs/aliases route `bridge-probe` to check-access while `bridge probe` means something else
findings.suggested_fix: Name the new command distinctly from the retained `bridge-probe` alias (e.g. `rebar bridge suggest-config` or fold it as `check-access --emit-config`), and record the disambiguation in the S8 criterion.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether `rebar bridge probe` discovers required-create-fields via createmeta (reversing the documented out-of-scope decision) or leaves `create_defaults` as hand-authored-only, and align S5/S8 accordingly.
evidence: Plan: 'Required-custom-field create failures are prevented by a per-project `create_defaults` block'

user-guide.md:621-629 — 'A `createmeta` pre-flight is deliberately out of scope ... rebar does not [query it]'; cites Sentry precedent for refusing to invent required-field values
findings.finding: S8's probe 'emits suggested config for every offline-discoverable axis' and S5 relies on a `create_defaults` block for required custom fields, but the plan does not reconcile this with the shipped, deliberate decision that Jira `createmeta` required-field discovery is out of scope — so how the probe DISCOVERS required-create-fields (the only axis needing createmeta) is an unaddressed capability question.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — `create_defaults` bullet and `rebar bridge probe` bullet; children S5, S8
scenarios: Operator expects `rebar bridge probe` to suggest a `create_defaults` block but required fields are only discoverable via the out-of-scope createmeta endpoint

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the replay give-up bound (e.g. stop after N unproductive hops or when no allowed transition advances toward the target status, then drift) so 'bounded' is a decision, not left to the executor.
evidence: 'attempt replay of rebar's own recorded hop sequence (anchored on Jira's current status, bounded give-up→drift)'
No numeric or rule-based definition of 'bounded' is given.
findings.finding: The transition replay is described as 'bounded give-up→drift' but the bound is never quantified (max hops, iteration cap, or timeout), leaving the executor to choose the give-up threshold.
findings.location: Approach section (transition replay) and S6; AC line 'A non-allowed transition is attempted by replay ... and, failing that, drifts'
scenarios: Executor must decide when replay gives up; an unbounded loop or an arbitrary cap could differ from intent.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a default such as: replay attempts at most the length of the recorded hop sequence and gives up (drifts) on the first hop with no allowed Jira transition.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify in S6 how the recorded local hop sequence is projected through the (collapsing, non-injective) status map to distinct Jira states and how the replay start is anchored when Jira's current status is not the image of any recorded hop (including the zero-effective-hop collapse case), so replay is well-defined before it falls back to drift.
evidence: value_maps.LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA is explicitly non-injective/collapsing: blocked->'In Progress', in_progress->'In Progress', closed/cancelled/deleted->'Done' — so consecutive distinct local hops can map to the SAME Jira state (a no-op hop) or the local sequence can carry states with no distinct Jira image

acli.transition_issue_by_name is issue-state-specific: it GETs the transitions available FROM the current state, matches by name/to.name, and raises when none reaches the target — so 'replay' must be resolved per current Jira state, not against a static map

plan says replay is 'anchored on Jira's current status' but does not state how the recorded local hops are converted to Jira-state hops or how the replay start index is chosen when Jira's current status has drifted off the mapped sequence
findings.finding: The S6 transition-replay mechanism does not specify how rebar's recorded LOCAL hop sequence is projected through the collapsing/non-injective status map onto a sequence of distinct Jira states, nor how replay locates its starting point when Jira's current status is not the image of any recorded local hop.
findings.location: Approach section ('attempt replay of rebar's own recorded hop sequence (anchored on Jira's current status, bounded give-up->drift)'); child S6; AC 'A non-allowed transition is attempted by replay of rebar's recorded hops'
scenarios: A ticket recorded locally as open->in_progress->blocked->in_progress, whose Jira issue is currently in 'Done' (drifted): the recorded hops all collapse onto {To Do, In Progress}, none of which is reachable-from/anchored-on the current 'Done' state
A collapse where blocked and in_progress both map to 'In Progress' produces a zero-length effective hop, so 'replay of hops' has nothing to enact yet the direct transition already failed
